title: Outbound: how does the draft claim suppress a concurrent double Send?
scope: Two Today tabs sending one draft, their separate sendAction calls, and the conditional Postgres UPDATE claiming its row.
omissions: Guards and Gmail/LinkedIn/X delivery after a successful claim
Conversation Send: each click inserts its own row, so no shared claim

groups.label: Owner's browser
groups.description: Local client: two tabs, one session

groups.label: AWS RDS
groups.description: Hosted, managed: us-west-1, TLS per docs

nodes.label: Today tab B
nodes.description: Same draft card, same Send; either may win

nodes.label: Postgres
nodes.description: First draft|failed UPDATE wins, per attempt

notes.title: Loser gets 0 rows: skipped, edits lost
notes.text: Each UPDATE autocommits with no isolation override (Postgres default READ COMMITTED): a concurrent loser waits on the row lock, re-checks, gets 0 rows → skipped; its edits drop, card hides.

notes.title: Suppression, not exactly-once
notes.text: Winner resolves only after guards and a delivery try. Guard fails and in-try throws reset it to failed (re-sendable), even if markSent threw after Gmail accepted; closed/replied → skipped.

notes.title: A crash after the claim strands the row
notes.text: A timeout (maxDuration 300) or a query throw outside the try leaves the row sending: Send/Skip can't claim it; email/LinkedIn rows count to the limit for 24h; only LinkedIn gets a 3h alert.
